sentences.en: We get support from UC Davis, a globally ranked university working to solve the world's most pressing problems in food, energy, health, education, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我们获得了加州大学戴维斯分校的支持，这是一所全球知名的大学，致力于解决世界在食品、能源、健康、教育和环境方面最紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: UC Davis researchers collaborate and innovate in California and around the globe to find transformational solutions.
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员在加州及全球各地开展合作与创新，以寻找变革性的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's all part of the university's mission to promote quality of life for all living things.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是该大学旨在提升所有生物生活质量的使命的一部分。

sentences.en: Find out more at 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu.
sentences.zh: 了解更多信息请访问 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: And this is Jeff Maino.
sentences.zh: 这位是杰夫·梅诺。

sentences.en: My name is Jeff Maino.
sentences.zh: 我叫杰夫·梅诺。

sentences.en: I'm an architecture writer and blogger based in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 我是一名base在洛杉矶的建筑作家和博主。

sentences.en: And for seven years, he has written a website called Building Blog.
sentences.zh: 七年来，他一直在运营一个名为“建筑博客”的网站。

sentences.en: Which is about architectural conjecture, urban speculation, and landscape futures.
sentences.zh: 该网站主要探讨建筑推测、城市设想和景观未来。

sentences.en: I've always liked the sounds of things and the acoustic nature of walking through the city,
sentences.zh: 我一直很喜欢事物的声音，以及穿梭于城市之中的声学质感，

sentences.en: or even just the sense that when you're walking down a hall that has really rich, lush wall coverings,
sentences.zh: 甚至仅仅是那种感觉：当你走在一条墙面装饰极其丰富、厚重的走廊里时，

sentences.en: the right side can sound totally different from the left side.
sentences.zh: 右侧的声音听起来可能与左侧完全不同。

sentences.en: I've just always been interested in those sorts of acoustic aspects of architectural space.
sentences.zh: 我一直对建筑空间的这种声学特性很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Most architects, if they design for sound, what they're actually designing to do is design for silence.
sentences.zh: 大多数建筑师如果在设计时考虑声音，他们实际想要实现的设计是追求安静。

sentences.en: They're designing to keep sound out of the environments.
sentences.zh: 他们的设计旨在将声音挡在环境之外。

sentences.en: They're designing to make sure that you don't hear the street sounds that are happening outside,
sentences.zh: 他们的设计确保你听不到外面发生的街道噪音，

sentences.en: or that you're insulated from cars driving by, or from the gravel plant up the road.
sentences.zh: 或者让你免受驶过汽车或路边砂石厂噪音的干扰。

sentences.en: So it's really an architecture of silence that people tend to be designing for.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们往往倾向于设计一种寂静的建筑。

sentences.en: But, you know, having said that, there was an interesting project a couple years ago by an architect named Joel Sanders.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，几年前有一位名叫乔尔·桑德斯的建筑师做过一个有趣的项目。

sentences.en: It was basically an architectural design.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一个建筑设计。

sentences.en: Instead of standard glass windows, it would use things like parabolic microphones.
sentences.zh: 它不使用标准的玻璃窗，而是采用抛物面麦克风之类的事物。

sentences.en: Kind of like those things that you see people holding on the sides of the football field during NFL games.
sentences.zh: 有点像你在美式橄榄球比赛中看到人们举在球场边的那种设备。

sentences.en: These parabolic microphones would be pointed at the sky, or they'd be pointed out into the woods nearby,
sentences.zh: 这些抛物面麦克风会指向天空，或者指向附近的树林，

sentences.en: or, you know, they would capture the sounds of airplanes flying overhead, or birds in the forest, or for that matter, kids down the road.
sentences.zh: 又或者，你知道的，它们会捕捉头顶飞过的飞机声、森林里的鸟鸣声，或是顺便记录路边小孩的声音。

sentences.en: It very consciously and clearly brings acoustics into the architectural equation.
sentences.zh: 它非常清醒且明确地将声学纳入了建筑方程式中。

sentences.en: There was an article in a British magazine called The Wire.
sentences.zh: 英国一本名为《The Wire》的杂志上曾刊登过一篇文章。

sentences.en: It was an article about generative sound, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 那是一篇关于所谓生成式音乐的文章。

sentences.en: It referred to this idea of a quote-unquote sound garden.
sentences.zh: 文中提到了一个所谓的“声音花园”的概念。

sentences.en: Rather than being the 1990s grunge band, they were talking actually about the idea that you would deliberately plant
sentences.zh: 他们指的不是20世纪90年代的垃圾摇滚乐队，而是关于这样一种想法：你刻意去种植

sentences.en: certain species of flowering trees and that kind of thing in your back garden,
sentences.zh: 某种开花树木以及诸如此类的植物在你的后花园里，

sentences.en: so that you could sort of time an acoustic event over the course of the year.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以在一年当中安排一场声学事件的发生。

sentences.en: There are certain species that when they bloom, the seed pod opens up with an audible pop.
sentences.zh: 某些品种在开花时，种荚会伴随着一声清脆的爆裂声打开。

sentences.en: It's kind of the acoustic equivalent of the daisies coming up through the ground, or the tulips blooming.
sentences.zh: 这有点像是雏菊破土而出或郁金香盛开的声学版。

sentences.en: There's all kinds of other species that have particularly kind of silky leaves that brush against each other in the breeze,
sentences.zh: 还有各种其他品种的植物拥有特别丝滑的叶子，在微风中互相摩挲，

sentences.en: so you can fall asleep at night to the sound of this kind of really silken, silvery, sort of tree-brushing sound.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在夜晚伴随着这种丝滑、银铃般、树叶摩擦的声音入睡。

sentences.en: That's one thing I think is really quite interesting, that you could actually deliberately sort of build an acoustic ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常有趣的一点是，你可以真正刻意地建造一个声学生态系统。

sentences.en: You know, you could easily imagine that sort of thing being added on to a kind of botanic garden
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你很容易想象这种东西会被添加到一个植物园里，

sentences.en: so that you'd pay money to go literally listen to plant life.
sentences.zh: 这样人们就会花钱专门去聆听植物的生命。

sentences.en: Jeff Mayno is also interested in archaeoacoustics.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·梅诺也对考古声学感兴趣。

sentences.en: Good question.
sentences.zh: 好问题。

sentences.en: It's basically the concern with, well, two things.
sentences.zh: 它基本上关注的是两个方面。

sentences.en: Not only how would a building have sounded, or what would have been the acoustic effect of a certain building
sentences.zh: 不仅是某栋建筑听起来会是怎样，或者当这座建筑矗立时，它会产生怎样的声学效果，

sentences.en: when that building was standing,
sentences.zh: 而且还包括特定文明或村庄的声音文化是怎样的。

sentences.en: but then also what was the sort of sound culture of a given civilization or village.
sentences.zh: 古玛雅神庙不仅被建造为壮观的山脉状建筑，

sentences.en: Old Mayan temples were built not just as spectacular mountain-like constructions,
sentences.zh: 而且专门被设计为声学设备，不仅能放大祭司的声音，

sentences.en: but specifically as acoustic devices that would amplify not only the voice of the priest,
sentences.zh: 还能放大诸如用来演奏仪式音乐的海螺等事物的声音。

sentences.en: but also the sounds of things like the conch shells that would be played
sentences.zh: 建筑在物理设计上实际上尽可能地具有回音效果。

sentences.en: to do ritualistic music and that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 建筑本身就像是声学共鸣器或低音炮，

sentences.en: The building was actually physically designed to be as echoey as possible.
sentences.zh: 它们被刻意制造出来，以帮助人们诱发一种几乎类似于迷幻状态的感觉。

sentences.en: The buildings themselves were like acoustic resonators or subwoofers, so to speak,
sentences.zh: 这就是考古声学。

sentences.en: that were deliberately made to help induce a kind of, almost like a psychedelic state in people.
sentences.zh: 它就像是印第安纳·琼斯遇到了约翰·凯奇。

sentences.en: That's archaeoacoustics.
sentences.zh: 我认为建筑师太愿意将声学和声音交给声音设计师去处理，

sentences.en: It's like Indiana Jones meets John Cage.
sentences.zh: 或者交由其他人负责。

sentences.en: I think architects are too willing to sort of let acoustics and sound be taken care of by sound designers
sentences.zh: 我认为如果能看到他们更多地思考如何将建筑融入城市的声景中，那将非常有趣。

sentences.en: or taken up by other people.
sentences.zh: 建筑界有很多关于如何建造具有语境特定性并真正回应其场地的讨论。

sentences.en: And I think it really would be interesting to see them think more in terms of
sentences.zh: 但所谓的“场地”几乎总是字面意义上的视觉问题。

sentences.en: how to integrate their building into the soundscape of a city.
sentences.zh: 这是与城市的一种光学关系。

sentences.en: There's a lot of talk within architecture of how to build something that's contextually specific
sentences.zh: 实际上，如果能考虑让建筑师去对他们建筑所在的街区进行声学测绘，

sentences.en: and really responds to its site.
sentences.zh: 然后找出一种好的干预方式，

sentences.en: But the site, quote-unquote, is almost always literally a question of sight.
sentences.zh: 并把这些声音反射回街区，那将非常有趣。

sentences.en: It's an optical relationship to the city.
sentences.zh: 过多的沉默并不比过多的噪音更有趣。

sentences.en: It would really be interesting, actually, to think about architects going out to sort of
sentences.zh: 本周的“99%隐形”由尼克·范德科尔克制作。

sentences.en: acoustically map the city block where their building is going to be
sentences.zh: 我是你的主持人罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: and then figuring out a nice way to intervene in it
sentences.zh: 本节目由Lunar赞助播出，

sentences.en: and maybe reflect those sounds back at the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 用创意创造改变。

sentences.en: Too much silence is no more interesting than too much noise.
sentences.zh: 这是KALW、美国建筑师学会旧金山分会以及建筑与设计中心的合作项目。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Nick Vanderkolk.
sentences.zh: 要了解更多信息，包括杰夫·梅诺的建筑博客的链接——

sentences.en: I'm your host, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 那是必读内容，你绝对应该去看看——

sentences.en: The program is made possible with support from Lunar,
sentences.zh: 还有尼克·范德科尔克的《爱与广播》，

sentences.en: making a difference with creativity.
sentences.zh: 这是他为voclo.org制作的一个节目，

sentences.en: It's a project of KALW, the American Institute of Architects San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 它令人惊叹、才华横溢且带有黑暗的迷人色彩。

sentences.en: and the Center for Architecture and Design.
sentences.zh: 尼克是该领域的声波创新者之一，绝对是最棒的。

sentences.en: To find out more, including links to Jeff Mano's building blog,
sentences.zh: 我本来打算在本节目结束时放一段节选，

sentences.en: which is essential reading, you should absolutely go there,
sentences.zh: 但是天哪，那个节目是给成年人看的，

sentences.en: and Nick Vanderkolk's Love and Radio,
sentences.zh: 而我有八年级的孩子在听这个节目。

sentences.en: which is a program he does for voclo.org,
sentences.zh: 我做不到。

sentences.en: and it's stunning and brilliant and darkly fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我真的做不到。

sentences.en: And Nick is one of the sonic innovators in the field, absolutely the beSt.
sentences.zh: 总之，你绝对应该去看看。

sentences.en: I was going to include an excerpt, actually, at the end of this program,
sentences.zh: 如果你是个成年人，你会喜欢它的。

sentences.en: but man, that program is for adults,
sentences.zh: 网址是loveandradio.org，

sentences.en: and I have eighth grade kids who listen to this.
sentences.zh: 你可以在99%invisible.org上找到它的链接。

sentences.en: I couldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I just couldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 我实在做不到。

sentences.en: Anyway, you should absolutely check it out.
sentences.zh: 总之，你绝对应该去看看。

sentences.en: If you're an adult, you'll love it.
sentences.zh: 如果你是成年人，你会爱上它的。

sentences.en: It's at loveandradio.org,
sentences.zh: 网址是 loveandradio.org，

sentences.en: and you'll find a link to that on 99%invisible.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 99%invisible.org 上找到它的链接。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。
